spec_title: Foundation — Schema, Roles, Permissions, Status Maps, Navigation
description: Establishes everything the rest of the migration stands on: the six-role enum, the user profile extensions, all request-lifecycle tables, the per-user permission grant table, the document-number generator, the status maps that name and colour every state, the role-aware sidebar entries, and the seeded accounts. No user-facing page ships here.

happy_path.action: prisma migrate runs the new models
happy_path.result: Request, AuditLog, RequestComment, Csm, DocumentSequence, UserPermission exist; Role gains four staff values; User gains position, signatureUrl, profileComplete
one active, email-verified account per role exists with role-default permissions granted
the sidebar shows only the destinations their role owns, and getDefaultRoute sends them to their landing page

happy_path.action: submits their first request of the year
happy_path.result: generateDocumentNumber issues YYYY-0001 and DocumentSequence.lastSequence becomes 1

alternate_paths.name: Concurrent submits
alternate_paths.trigger: two users submit in the same second of the same year
alternate_paths.result: the transactional upsert+increment issues two distinct numbers; no duplicate, no gap

alternate_paths.name: Year rolls over
alternate_paths.result: a new DocumentSequence row is created for the new year and numbering restarts at 0001

alternate_paths.name: Role changed by admin
alternate_paths.result: permissions are wiped and reseeded from the new role's defaults, so a demoted director keeps nothing

models.name: Role
models.prisma_note: Enum in prisma/models/user.prisma — adds the four staff roles to the existing USER/ADMIN pair

models.name: Action
models.prisma_note: New enum in prisma/models/user-permission.prisma — the seven grantable capabilities

models.name: User
models.prisma_note: Extends prisma/models/user.prisma. role loses its bare type and gains @default(USER); status default flips to inactive so an admin activates staff deliberately

models.name: Request
models.prisma_note: New model in prisma/models/request.prisma — the core entity. The five *Status columns are deliberately separate: masterStatus is what the requestor sees, the others are per-stage state a reviewer's guard reads

models.name: AuditLog
models.prisma_note: New model in prisma/models/request.prisma — one row per action taken on a request. It is the only history the app has; nothing overwrites it

models.name: RequestComment
models.prisma_note: New model in prisma/models/request.prisma — the requestor/processor conversation. Cascades on request delete

models.name: Csm
models.prisma_note: New model in prisma/models/csm.prisma — the satisfaction record, created by the final director approval and completed by the requestor

models.name: DocumentSequence
models.prisma_note: New model in prisma/models/request.prisma — one row per calendar year, holding the last issued sequence

models.name: UserPermission
models.prisma_note: New model in prisma/models/user-permission.prisma — a per-user grant of one Action. Role decides the DEFAULTS; this table is the truth

trpc_procedures.name: generateDocumentNumber
trpc_procedures.description: Atomically upserts the current year's DocumentSequence with lastSequence increment inside a transaction and returns YYYY-NNNN, zero-padded to four digits. Exported as a plain helper too, because request.submit calls it inline rather than over the wire.

navigation_config.description: Replaces the template's Dashboard/Admin/Profile items with the IRMS destinations. getNavigation filters by role; the sidebar only ORGANISES — every route also carries a server-side role gate.

seeder.strategy: upsert on email — idempotent, safe to re-run, never resets a changed password
seeder.password_note: Hashed with better-auth's own hashPassword from better-auth/crypto, the same function the sign-up path uses
post_steps: seedUserPermissions(user.id, role, user.id) for every seeded account so each lands with its role defaults
emailVerified: true on every seeded account — the auth guard bounces an unverified user to /verify-email and there is no mail provider wired

functional: Role has exactly six values: USER, ADMIN, IDO_OFFICER, IDO_CHAIRPERSON, DIRECTOR, BUDGET_OFFICER.
src/utils/config.ts USER_ROLES lists all six, so UserRole stays the single source for role typing across nav, routes and auth functions.

src/lib/permissions.ts exports ALL_ACTIONS, ACTION_LABELS (label + description per action, used by the admin permissions modal), ROLE_DEFAULT_PERMISSIONS, seedUserPermissions, resetAndSeedPermissions and assertPermission.

ROLE_DEFAULT_PERMISSIONS: USER = CREATE_REQUEST, SUBMIT_REQUEST, ADD_COMMENT, SUBMIT_CSM; IDO_OFFICER and IDO_CHAIRPERSON = ADD_COMMENT, REVIEW_REQUEST; BUDGET_OFFICER = ADD_COMMENT, APPROVE_BUDGET; DIRECTOR = ADD_COMMENT, APPROVE_DIRECTOR; ADMIN = none.
assertPermission(userId, action) reads UserPermission and throws FORBIDDEN when the grant is absent. Role is never consulted at action time — only at grant time.
src/lib/status-maps/request-status.ts exports masterStatusMap (label + AppChip tone per masterStatus), idoEvaluationStatusMap, MASTER_STATUS_OPTIONS and FILTER_OPTIONS.

masterStatusMap covers DRAFT, SUBMITTED, RETURNED, UNDER_IDO_REVIEW, UNDER_DIRECTOR_REVIEW, UNDER_IDO_FINAL_REVIEW, UNDER_FINAL_DIRECTOR_REVIEW, APPROVED, FOR_NEXT_YEAR_PPMP, REJECTED_BY_IDO, BUDGET_OFFICER_REJECTED, DIRECTOR_REJECTED, IDO_FINAL_REJECTED, FINAL_REJECTED, COMPLETED.
The FINAL_REJECTED label reads 'Director Final Rejected', not 'Final Rejected' — it was the fix logged in IRMS-old TASKS.md and must not regress.
Chip tones come from ChipTone (default | accent | success | warning | danger), never a raw colour, because AppChip takes a tone.
generateDocumentNumber runs inside prisma.$transaction with upsert + increment, and formats as `${year}-${String(lastSequence).padStart(4, '0')}`.

src/routes/_authenticated.tsx passes mainWidth from the matched route's staticData.mainWidth into AppLayout, defaulting to 'default' — the frame already accepts the prop and nothing currently feeds it.
The seed creates one account per role, all active and email-verified, with role-default permissions granted.
authorization: roleProcedure(...roles) in src/integrations/trpc/init.ts is the only role gate; it already exists and now accepts the four new Role values with no change.

protectedProcedure additionally loads the user's status and throws FORBIDDEN unless it is 'active' — a suspended account keeps a valid session but can do nothing. This is an addition to the template's protectedProcedure.
assertAuthenticatedRoleFn (src/features/auth/functions/auth.functions.ts) validates against all six roles via USER_ROLES, so a route gate cannot name a role the enum does not have.
No page-level gate replaces a procedure-level gate. A user can always deep-link; the router is what refuses.
ux: Sidebar entries are role-filtered so nobody sees a destination that will bounce them, but the filter is convenience, not security.
Role label under the wordmark says what the person is ('Campus Director'), not what the enum is ('DIRECTOR').
Status colours are consistent everywhere they appear — a chip in a table, a chip in the timeline and a chip on the detail page all read masterStatusMap.

rules.zod_rule: keyof typeof USER_ROLES — six literal keys, no string fallback

server_guards.error: FORBIDDEN — Your account is not active. Please contact an administrator.

server_guards.guard: ctx.user.role is in the allowed list
a UserPermission row exists for (userId, action)
server_guards.error: FORBIDDEN — You don't have permission to perform this action
none — the transaction is the guard against duplicate numbers

covers: ROLE_DEFAULT_PERMISSIONS grants a USER exactly CREATE_REQUEST, SUBMIT_REQUEST, ADD_COMMENT, SUBMIT_CSM
ROLE_DEFAULT_PERMISSIONS grants ADMIN nothing — an admin manages accounts and never touches a request
assertPermission resolves when the grant row exists
assertPermission throws FORBIDDEN when the grant row is absent, even for a user whose ROLE would have it by default
resetAndSeedPermissions deletes every existing grant before inserting the new role's defaults
every masterStatus written by any procedure in specs 005-015 has an entry in masterStatusMap
every entry's tone is one of the five ChipTone values
first call of a year returns YYYY-0001
a new year creates its own DocumentSequence row and restarts at 0001
two concurrent calls return two different numbers
getNavigation('USER') returns My Requests and New Request and not the staff dashboard
getNavigation('IDO_OFFICER') returns the staff dashboard only
getDefaultRoute returns a route the role's navigation actually contains, for all six roles

acceptance_criteria.when: npm run db:migrate and npm run db:seed are run
acceptance_criteria.then: six accounts exist, one per role, all active and emailVerified, each holding its role's default permissions

acceptance_criteria.given: the current year is 2026 and no request has been submitted
acceptance_criteria.then: it returns 2026-0001 and DocumentSequence for 2026 has lastSequence 1

acceptance_criteria.given: a user whose status is 'suspended' holds a valid session
acceptance_criteria.then: the call fails with FORBIDDEN and the message names the account state, not the endpoint

acceptance_criteria.given: a BUDGET_OFFICER whose APPROVE_BUDGET grant has been revoked by an admin
acceptance_criteria.then: assertPermission throws FORBIDDEN even though their ROLE would grant it by default
it shows Dashboard and Profile only — no My Requests, no Accounts

edge_cases: Two simultaneous submits in the same year must not produce duplicate document numbers — the upsert + increment must be inside prisma.$transaction, never a read-then-write.
documentNumber must never be regenerated once set — request.submit reads the existing value first and only generates when it is null, so a RETURNED request keeps its number on resubmit.
Changing a user's role must reset permissions rather than merge them — a director demoted to USER must not keep APPROVE_DIRECTOR.
Role must default to USER at the database level, never null — a null role breaks every navigation filter and every gate.
Adding enum values to Role is a destructive-looking migration on Postgres; generate the migration and check it does not rewrite the users table before applying it in production.

User.status default changes from 'active' (template) to 'inactive'; the seed and the admin-created accounts set 'active' explicitly, and self sign-up (spec 002) must decide deliberately which it wants.
out_of_scope: Every page — this spec is schema, config and helpers only.
The request lifecycle procedures — each stage owns its own spec (010-014).
The admin UI for granting permissions — spec 017.
Email verification delivery — no mail provider is wired; the seed sidesteps it with emailVerified: true.
Migrating existing IRMS-old data — this is a fresh build, not a data migration.
